thread:
maria: Heads-up — while investigating a quotas bug I found that the admin CSV export (daily) contains usage rows across multiple tenants. Looks like a tenant filter wasn't applied. :rotating_light:
kevin: Can you repro and share the exact export path / job id?
maria: Repro steps: go to Console > Billing > Exports -> download latest csv. Job id 0x3f (quota-exporter). Sample rows attached (trimmed): tenant_id values: 123, 456, 789. This should be tenant-scoped.
rachel: Wait — we rolled the RBAC role refactor on 3/8 (global->scoped changes). Might be related.
maria: Audit shows the export called by service-account:quota-exporter@infra.svc. Audit record: audit-bot: "EXPORT_START user=svc:quota-exporter target=s3://redwood-exports/billing/2026-03-20.csv"
kevin: Can you paste the query the exporter runs?
maria: Here it is (redacted):
```sql
SELECT org_id, usage_tokens, cost_cents, timestamp
FROM billing_usage_summary
-- MISSING WHERE org_id = $EXPORT_TENANT_ID
ORDER BY timestamp DESC
LIMIT 100000
```
kevin: Yep, missing tenant filter. That should've been injected by the job wrapper.
kevin: Quick mitigation: disable scheduled export job, rotate presigned URLs, and revoke the service-account's S3 PutObject perms.
tom: I'll take the hotfix for the exporter binary — add tenant_id filter + add server-side tenant validation (server must assert org_id == requestor.org). I'll push a patch to run ASAP.
ajay: Also, heads-up on encryption: the CSV was written to S3 encrypted with a KMS key (alias/redwood-exports). Key policy currently allows decrypt for infra-service-role and some tooling CI. We need to restrict decrypt rights and rotate the key because it's now tied to a potential data exposure.
sally: I'll open an incident and notify CS about impacted customers. Suggest conservative outreach: only those with confirmed exposure.
maria: Any PII in the export? Looks like only org_id, usage_tokens, cost_cents, timestamp — but cost + org mapping could be sensitive.
kevin: Forensics: check CloudTrail for GetObject on that S3 path — see who downloaded. audit-bot: "S3:GetObject by user=billing-ops@redwood internal at 1803456805"
kevin: Good catch, audit shows a billing-ops download at 1803456805. Could be internal debugging; still a leak.
ajay: Action items: 1) tom: hotfix and deploy exporter to enforce tenant scoping. 2) kevin: revoke service-account S3 PutObject and rotate KMS key; update key policy to deny cross-account decryption and require attribute:PrincipalTag org_id equals bucket owner. 3) sally: incident ticket + customer comms. 4) maria: collect example rows and preserve evidence.
kevin: For KMS rotation, timeline: rotate within 2 hours, revoke grants immediately. I'll coordinate with infra to ensure no other exports break.
tom: Pushing patch to branch hotfix/export-tenant-filter and running unit tests now. Will do canary deploy to prod export workers. deploy-bot: "Canary deploy started for job=quota-exporter image=infra/quota-exporter:hotfix-180345 - 1803456920"
infra-bot: "Disabled scheduled export rule: exports-daily-03:00 UTC by user=maria at 1803456940"
sally: Opened incident INC-2026-307 in PagerDuty — assigned to sec-ops. I'll draft a customer note template.
maria: I'm attaching sample rows & the exact CSV path to the incident ticket.
kevin: After hotfix and rotation, we'll run a full scan for other export jobs (reporting/exporter, audit-logs export, analytics export) to ensure they all enforce tenant scoping.
ajay: Also double-check KMS key grants used by CI. We likely need to add a condition on aws:PrincipalTag to ensure keys only decrypt for roles scoped to the org.
kevin: One more: add an RBAC unit test to prevent regressions — tests should fail if an exporter can request results without tenant constraint.
tom: Agreed. I'll add integration tests that assert the server rejects exports when the caller's org != row.org_id.
sally: Timeline summary in incident: hotfix deployed 1803456980, KMS rotate started 1803457005, exports disabled 1803456940, customer comms draft by 1803457200.
maria: Thanks all. Keep updates here and link to INC-2026-307. :eyes:
kevin: I'll post a postmortem once we finish root-cause analysis and remediation steps.
kevin: Also recommend a short-term guard: block any bulk CSV downloads from Console until we validate export tooling.
kevin: cc @security-leads
